data.name: Andreas
data.gender_notes: Andreas is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name 'Andros', which means 'man' or 'masculine'. In the New Testament, Saint Andrew was a fisherman and a disciple of Jesus. He is the patron saint of Russia and Romania. The name Andreas carries the meaning “Man, masculine” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Andreas usually hope their child will grow to embody man, masculine and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Andreas belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Man, masculine.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Andreas total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: אנדריאס
in_hebrew.meaning: השם אנדריאס נגזר מהשם היווני ופירושו גבר חזק וגבור
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אנדריאס הוא נגזרת של השם היווני 'אנδρέας' (Andreas), שמקורו במילה היוונית 'אנδρός' (andros), שפירושו גבר או גבור. השם אנדריאס הוא שם נפוץ בקרב הנוצרים, ויש לו קונוטציות של חוזק, גבורה וגבריות. השם מופיע בברית החדשה, ויש לו חשיבות רבה במסורת הנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Ανδρέας
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Ανδρέας σημαίνει ισχυρός και γενναίος άνθρωπος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ανδρέας προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'ανδρός' (andros), που σημαίνει άντρας ή γενναίος. Ο Άνδρέας ήταν ένας από τους δώδεκα αποστόλους του Ιησού Χριστού και ήταν ο πρώτος που ακολούθησε τον Ιησού. Το όνομα Ανδρέας είναι πολύ δημοφιλές στην Ελλάδα και έχει μεγάλη σημασία στην Ορθοδόξο Εκκλησία.

in_latin.name: Andreas
in_latin.meaning: Andreas nomen significat virum fortem et robustum
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Andreas derivatur ex verbo Graeco 'ανδρός' (andros), quod significat virum vel robustum. Andreas fuit unus ex duodecim apostolis Iesu Christi et primus qui Iesum secutus est. Nomen Andreas est nomen sanctum et habet magnam significationem in traditione Christiana.

in_english.name: Andreas
in_english.meaning: Andreas means strong, manly, and courageous
in_english.long_meaning: The name Andreas is derived from the Greek word 'ανδρός' (andros), meaning man or male. It is a popular name in Christian tradition, associated with Saint Andrew, one of Jesus' twelve apostles. The name Andreas symbolizes strength, courage, and masculinity, and is widely used across various Christian cultures.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Andreas' holds significant cultural importance, especially in Eastern European countries like Russia and Romania. Saint Andrew is revered as their patron saint, and many towns, churches, and institutions bear his name. The name is also common among people of Greek and Scottish descent.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Saint Andrew was an early disciple of Jesus and is believed to have introduced Christianity to the lands of the Black Sea. His steadfastness and dedication to disseminating the teachings of Jesus make the name Andreas spiritually significant. It is often given to boys with the hope that they will embody the virtues of faith, commitment, and resilience that Andrew showed throughout his life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Andreas: Greek origin meaning "man, warrior." Symbolically, it represents courage, strength, and masculinity. Spiritually, it is a reminder to stand firm in faith and face challenges with bravery.

biblical_reference.note: Andrew was one of Jesus' twelve apostles

historical_references.reference: Andreas Cappelanus was a Cardinal of the Roman Catholic Church who became the Archbishop of Ravenna and Primate of Venice in 1484. He played an important role in the political intrigues of the late 15th century Italian city-states and was a noted patron of of the arts.

Andreas of Crete, also known as Andreas the Giant of Crete, was a monk and hermit who is recognized as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church. He lived between the 10th and 11th centuries and is most famous for his legendary strength and asceticism.
